carbon_policy_signal.item: Populist surge threatens to unwind EU climate policy consensus post-COP31; Spain snap election (late November 2026) poses conservative victory risk to EU ETS enforcement and electrification targets.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Conservative election victory in Spain would relax climate policy enforcement and decelerate power decarbonization urgency, pressuring EUA valuations and multi-year carbon curve on weaker demand assumptions.

freshness_caveat: Coal (320 days old, as of 2025-12-26) and Clean Dark (315 days old, as of 2025-12-31) are stale; recent analysis relies on current renewables, GB/DE power, TTF, and storage data only.
risk_flags: Renewable share at 11.2% (2nd-percentile, -77.35% MoM) forces coal and gas back into merit; Clean Spark at 94th-percentile (48.91 EUR/MWh) reflects fuel-switch extremity.

GB Power at 95th-percentile (208.97 EUR/MWh) vs. DE Power at 90th-percentile (231.29 EUR/MWh) creates arbitrage tension; UK-EU interconnector deal nearing completion could compress spread via cross-Channel capacity.
EU Storage 17.2pp below seasonal average at 72% full; refill pace into winter will set H2 thermal call and TTF upside risk if weather turns cold.
Spain snap election in late November 2026 poses downside to EU climate policy enforcement; conservative victory would relax decarbonization rules and pressures EUA curve and power demand forecasts.

base.summary: Renewables recovery modest; thermal stack stays high; GB-EU spread narrows gradually on interconnector progress.

downside.summary: Renewable recovery accelerates; UK-EU interconnector finalized with full arbitrage capacity; Spain conservative election relaxes climate demand.

upside.summary: Cold front + renewable lows persist; storage refill slows; Mediterranean gas corridor escalation tightens supply certainty.

themes: Renewables collapse lifting thermal merit order
GB power premium and UK-EU interconnector arbitrage risk
Storage deficit tightening winter refill trajectory
Populist election threat to EU climate policy consensus
top_drivers: Renewable share collapse to 2nd-percentile (11.2%) forces thermal stack to extreme merit; coal & gas dispatch elevated, fueling Clean Spark 94th-percentile (48.91 EUR/MWh).
GB power 95th-percentile (208.97 EUR/MWh) vs. continental 90th-percentile (231.29 EUR/MWh); UK-EU interconnector deal threatens arbitrage compression and spread narrowing.
EU storage 17.2pp below seasonal average; winter refill pace and cold weather will amplify thermal call and TTF front-curve extension risk.
top_takeaway: Renewables at 2nd-percentile collapse drives thermal stack into merit; GB power at 95th-percentile premium widens fuel-switch risk vs. continent; storage 17pp below seasonal average tightens winter refill.

watchlist.why: At 2nd-percentile (11.2%), extreme scarcity drives coal and gas dispatch; thermal stack extension amplifies power and carbon price sensitivity to weather recovery.
GB premium (95th vs. 90th-percentile) likely to compress as UK-EU interconnector finalization increases cross-Channel arbitrage capacity and price convergence.
At 17.2pp below seasonal average (72% full); winter injection patterns will signal thermal demand intensity and TTF front-curve sustainability into Q1 2027.
Conservative victory would weaken EU climate policy consensus and signal multi-year EUA and power-curve downside; polling tightens climate-policy enforcement credibility.
Within typical range (84.73 EUR/MWh) but weekly -11.87% suggests softness; Mediterranean geopolitical tension (Turkey-Greece) is asymmetric tail-risk to alternative LNG import routes.
